Issued at 356 PM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Currently...

Conditions across the area continue to sound like a broken  
record...dry, with well above normal temperatures. Looking 
aloft...upper air and satellite data continue to show
southwesterly flow in place across the Central Plains this 
afternoon. This is driven by upper level riding extending north 
from the eastern Srn Plains northward toward the western Great 
Lakes...set up between one area of low pressure working its way 
east through the Midwest, and troughing set up along the West 
Coast. At the surface, lower pressure sits over eastern portions
of CO...with a trough axis/cold front extending northeast 
through SW-North central NE into eastern SD. This sfc boundary 
being in closer to proximity to the local forecast area is 
helping keep winds from being as strong/widespread as it was on 
Saturday. Seeing quite a range across the forecast area...with 
ODX/LXN on the light/variable to at times calm side, vs gusts 
exceeding 30 MPH across far SSE portions of the area. Had more 
widespread coverage of upper level clouds to start the day...but
that has diminished/pushed east with time...leaving mostly 
sunny skies for most of the area this afternoon. Hasn't been any
big surprises as far as temperatures go...if anything, those 
far NNW locations may fall a few degrees short, with other 
locations solidly in the mid-upper 80s to low 90s (SSE areas).

Tonight through Monday Night...

Through this more immediate, short-term period through Monday 
night...most the far majority of the forecast area, it will
continue to be a dry period. Models are in good agreement with
not showing any notable change in the overall upper level 
flow...remaining southwesterly. The upper level high/ridge axis 
shifts a bit further east...while the main low pressure system 
becomes more centered roughly over southern NV. A piece of 
shortwave energy riding around the edge of the ridging into the 
Dakotas late tonight and moreso during the day on Monday...the 
main impact for our area being the sfc frontal boundary gets 
more of push. Still some uncertainties with the exact timing of 
the front/where it ends up by the end of the day...which could 
potentially really throw a wrench in the wind/high temperature 
forecast. At this point, the forecast remains on the warmer 
side...with increasing mixing into warmer air aloft ahead of the
front allowing more more areas to potentially reach into the 
low 90s (mainly central/southeastern two-thirds of the area). 
Expecting another day with plenty of sun around...and until that
boundary pushes further in...gusty winds will be possible out 
ahead of it. Afternoon relative humidity values falling to 
near/below 30 will be possible once again, bringing another 
round of at least elevated fire weather concerns.

If there is going to be any preciptiation through this time
frame, it looks to come mid-evening Monday into the pre-dawn 
hours Tuesday...confined to far ESE portions of the area. A few 
models continue to show the potential for some 
isolated/scattered precip developing along the nose of increased
warm-air advection/lift...because there isn't a ton of support 
from other models, kept chances confined to 20 percent.

Tuesday through Thursday....

Better chances for precipitation finally work their way into the 
region as we get into the mid-week period...but there are still
some uncertainties with the timing...and overall coverage, 
especially early on. During the day on Tuesday...the main upper 
level low pressure system is still working its way east through 
the Desert SW/Rockies...with the surface frontal boundary 
expected to continue its gradual southward push. Big question 
for later Tuesday afternoon into the evening hours will be 
driven by where that surface front ends up...as it looks to be 
the focus for thunderstorm development. Forecast precipitation 
chances are still on the broad side into the evening-overnight 
hours Tuesday because of some of those lingering questions with 
location...the highest chances of 60+ percent remain across 
roughly the southeastern third of the forecast area. Some better
instability will work its way in ahead of the front...not out 
of the question that some storms could be strong/severe...and 
the SPC Day 3 Marginal Risk area continues to clip our SErn 
corner. 

While forecast precipitation chances remain area-wide, late
Tuesday night into the day on Wednesday brings a bit of a lull
in chances...before ramping back up Wednesday evening into 
Thursday. These increased chances are driven by the passage of 
the main upper low itself...crossing right over the area at some
point during the day on Thursday. Just how quickly that occurs 
and precip ends remains a little uncertain...GFS remains on the 
quicker side vs the ECMWF. Not talking about a significant 
difference...more on the scale of 6hrs or so...both have QPF 
gone by 06Z Friday.
